The learner asks specifically: Make sure one of the senses is this meaning: having a lot to do.

draft.emotion: hurried and focused, with too much to finish before the day ends
notes: Often used with the verb 'etmek' ('meşgul etmek' = to keep someone busy or take up their time) and 'olmak' ('meşgul olmak' = to be busy with, taking 'ile' / '-(y)le').
Takes front-vowel suffixes despite ending in the back vowel 'u' (e.g., 'meşgulüm' = I am busy).

senses.definition: Of a person: having a lot to do; occupied with work or an activity.

examples.translation: I am very busy today, let's meet in the evening.
examples.emotion: apologetic and rushed, explaining why there is no time right now

senses.definition: Of a telephone line or place: currently in use by someone else.

examples.text: Seni aradım ama telefonun sürekli meşgul çalıyor.
examples.translation: I called you, but your phone keeps ringing busy.

draftBefore.emotion: hurried and focused, with too much to finish before the day ends
notes: Meşgul is commonly used to describe someone who has a lot of work or tasks to handle at the moment.
It can also mean that a phone line or a physical space is currently occupied or in use.

senses.definition: Having a lot to do; actively doing something or caught up in work.

examples.translation: I am very busy today, let's meet in the evening.
examples.emotion: apologetic and rushed, explaining why there is no time right now

senses.definition: In use by someone else, such as a telephone line or a restroom.

examples.text: Telefonu aradım ama sürekli meşgul çalıyor.
